scenario.title: Crushing the Mutiny
intro.text:
CRUSHING THE MUTINY - 24 APR 1944

At sea off Alexandria, Egypt

Bad news from Egypt! A pro-EAM (National Liberation Front of Greece) mutiny inside the Greek Navy and the first Greek Brigade is broke out. Your troops are shipped from Palestine to Alexandria and help to down the revolt!

GOAL Capture all VH!

NOTE In this mission the AI has the first turn!
player.speaker: Commander
line.reaction-12-0-briliant.speaker: Major Edward Hale
line.reaction-12-0-briliant.text: Ruweisat and Deir el Mreir fell before the Axis line could adjust to the main offensive. The Greek contingent has earned the dangerous privilege of being useful to every political plan for liberation.
line.reaction-12-1-victory-tactical.text: The assigned objectives were taken and the Axis position is withdrawing. The formation has proved it can fight again; now every claimant to Greece asks whom that force obeys.
line.callback-0.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.callback-0.text: You kept the formation under government command when leaving might have felt cleaner. I defended that as duty. The wire around these Greek barracks is where the defence becomes difficult.
line.callback-1.speaker: Eleni Markou
line.callback-1.text: Cairo's orders now call us deserters. The fishing captain is ready for the road home. Hale's sentries, unfortunately, are ready as well.
line.callback-2.speaker: Major Edward Hale
line.callback-2.text: The Crete carriers remained together and became the formation's unofficial proof that retreat could still preserve skill.
line.callback-3.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.callback-3.text: The Crete transport pool vanished into the core. Its veterans are everywhere and therefore receive credit nowhere.
line.scene-0.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.scene-0.text: The rifles are stacked inside the wire, but nobody has surrendered the keys to the armoury. Half the sentries wear no belts. The other half have loaded magazines hidden in their tunics.
line.scene-1.speaker: Major Edward Hale
line.scene-1.text: The Eastern Harbour, wireless station, and arsenals must be under control before dark. If the committees talk to one another tonight, tomorrow we clear every barracks separately.
line.scene-2.speaker: Georgios Papandreou
line.scene-2.text: You remained with the government because an army requires lawful command. I will not prove that claim by treating every conscript behind this wire as an enemy.
line.scene-3.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.scene-3.text: Some followed a committee. Some followed their company because that was where breakfast was. Arrest the first group as if it were the second and by morning there will be only one group.
line.decision.speaker: Major Edward Hale
line.decision.text: Do we take the command points in one stroke, or open unit-by-unit surrender corridors and accept the delay?
line.decision.choice.seize-the-command-n: Strike first at the harbour, arsenals, and wireless stations.
Give infantry and anti-tank formations 15 experience and fully rearm the core.
line.decision.choice.open-surrender-corr: Offer unit-by-unit surrender, protect the hospital, and isolate only those who keep fighting.
Spend 100 prestige, restore the core to at least nine strength, and fully refuel it.
line.choice-a-0.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.choice-a-0.text: Then the first shot had better be at a lock, not a window. These are Greek barracks, even when the wrong men hold the keys.
line.choice-a-1.speaker: Major Edward Hale
line.choice-a-1.text: Harbour, wireless, arsenals—in that order. Once they are isolated, each unit gets one instruction to stand down. No freelance reprisals.
line.choice-b-0.speaker: Georgios Papandreou
line.choice-b-0.text: Negotiation will be called weakness in Cairo and betrayal in some of my own ministries. I accept that. I do not accept terms which leave armed committees in command.
line.choice-b-1.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.choice-b-1.text: The terms will name an hour, a collection point, and what happens to the men afterward. If we ask them to trust the government, the government must sign its name.
